claims.title: Why do independently chosen period witnesses agree?
claims.hypotheses: At one de Rham frame both integral witnesses satisfy the scalar and twisted conditions at order m, for the same correction.
claims.statement: The cross-multiplied difference of two witnesses is divisible entrywise by Eᵐ. The normalized residue at order m is independent of the choices.

claims.title: How do the witnesses define an invertible matrix over the de Rham valuation ring?
claims.hypotheses: Integral witnesses exist for every order on the same frame. The positive de Rham period ring is complete and separated for its residue uniformizer.
claims.statement: The scalar-normalized classes yield a unique invertible matrix B with residue the identity and Δ_g g(B)=B.

claims.title: Which columns give an invariant basis, and what bounds their poles?
claims.hypotheses: A height-N integral de Rham frame has an invertible Witt period matrix, its bounded-poles lifts and the primitive period relation.
claims.statement: Multiplying the corrected Frobenius period matrix by the indicated scalar gives an invariant basis Q_f. Its poles and the poles of its inverse have order at most N.

claims.title: How can witnesses with different scalar residues determine one matrix?
claims.hypotheses: A generator acts on the variable of the power-series ring by multiplication by a unit, and a single square-zero matrix defines the correction.
claims.statement: The witness with perturbation in degree d has defect equal to its scalar times (wᵈ−1)tᵈJ. An infinite-order multiplier distinguishes insufficient precision from a change of scalar residue.

claims.title: How can frames of different ranks be compared in one coordinate system?
claims.hypotheses: A projected tower with equivariant transitions is equipped with integral preframes of a common height. The target rank is fixed, and each level projects equivariantly onto the target modulo the prescribed power of ℓ.
claims.statement: One invertible Witt matrix gives common target coordinates at all levels. The rectangular comparison and its right inverse modulo ℓⁿ have entries in the étale coefficient ring.

claims.title: Which part of a layer can every deeper layer still represent?
claims.hypotheses: In these fixed coordinates each layer has the same bound H on its period matrix and inverse. The integral coefficient inclusion has a linear retraction.
claims.statement: For every precision n, one exponent c carries the entire integral image at level n into the image at every deeper level after multiplication by the evaluated variable to power c.

claims.title: Why do the images stop shrinking at each fixed precision?
claims.hypotheses: The residue field k is finite, the comparison maps preserve successive images modulo each fixed power of ℓ, and one power of the variable works at all deeper levels.
claims.statement: At each precision the images from the deeper layers eventually stabilize. Membership is detected by tuples of truncated power series over the corresponding finite Witt quotient.

claims.title: Can a vector that survives at one precision be lifted through every precision?
claims.hypotheses: At each precision the images stabilize, and the ambient Witt ring is adically complete and separated.
claims.statement: For each n a level m works for all starting columns: each such column lifts modulo ℓⁿ to a limit vector representable at every other precision by integral coefficients on that level.

claims.title: Why can the surviving columns be chosen to form a basis?
claims.hypotheses: The rectangular comparisons have right inverses modulo each power of ℓ over the étale coefficient ring, and their period matrices have bounded poles.
claims.statement: Surviving columns can be chosen to form a basis over the étale coefficient ring. Their image under the period comparison times τᴴ is integral.
